Welcome to Sellincourt Primary School
Welcome to Sellincourt Primary School. We are committed to respect and value the rights of others and encourage self-belief.
We promote consideration, compassion, honesty and trust whilst developing responsible and independent learners. We have high expectations of our children and are committed to each child reaching their full potential.
The Governors and staff of Sellincourt Primary School fully recognise the responsibilities and duty placed upon them to have arrangements to safeguard and promote the welfare of all pupils at the school. We recognise that all staff, including volunteers, have a full and active part to play in protecting pupils from harm.
If you need to contact a Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) at Sellincourt Primary School at anytime including out of hours and during weekends and holidays please email:
safeguarding@sellincourt.wandsworth.sch.uk
Please click here to see the areas of our School available to hire
Please click here for instructions on how to download our School Website App
You are now able to follow Sellincourt Primary School on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/sellincourtpri1/
Ofsted Report
Sellincourt School is a Good School
Learning
Welcome to Sellincourt Primary School

Fundamental British Values
Fundamental Values
The DfE has recently reinforced the need ‘to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote fundamental British values.’ These should form part of the SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural) education. The Government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 ‘Prevent’ Strategy, and these values were reiterated in November 2014. They are defined as democracy, the rule of law, equality of opportunity, freedom of speech, and the rights of all men and women to live free from persecution of any kind.
We believe that these are fundamental values and at Sellincourt we draw on the rich diversity of our community to help children understand and appreciate the wide range of cultural influences that have shaped modern Britain and how these values can be promoted. We encourage all children to be tolerant and respectful of each other's rights to hold differing faiths and beliefs and reinforce Democracy.

pageCache.text:
After School Care/Breakfast Club
OFSTED UNIQUE REFERENCE NUMBER: 101019
OFSTED REGISTRATION DATE: 1/9/2012
In order to register to attend either club please visit:
https://sellincourtprimary.magicbooking.co.uk
Please create a new account.
Sellincourt Primary School runs a wrap-around care service for parents. Early Birds is the Breakfast Club and The Cuckoo Club is the After School Care provision.
Cukoo Club Booking Launch Day Early Birds Club
Wednesday 15th July 2026 at 12.00pm
Early Birds Club
Early Birds Club is run from 7.30am to 9am every morning, Monday to Friday. The children are provided with a selection of cereals and toast for breakfast. They have a variety of activities provided in the morning which range from reading, drawing, games, and construction. Children are encouraged to be independent.
7.30 - 9.00 am: £6.50 per session
Daily ad hoc rate: £10.50 per session (correct cash accepted and receipted on day)
Cuckoo Club
The Cuckoo Club runs from 3.30pm to 6.15pm each school night, excluding the last day of each full term (Christmas, Easter, and Summer). Children are provided with a light snack at around 4.15pm, when other school clubs have finished. There is a wide variety of activities that are offered to the children often based around a theme or cultural celebration such as Diwali or Christmas. Other activities include indoor and outdoor games, puzzles, books, toys, and construction materials.
3.30 - 6.15 pm: £16.00 per session
Daily ad hoc rate: £20 per session (correct cash accepted and receipted on day)
Sibling discounts:
1 – child – full price / 2 - children – 25% discount / 3 – children – 25% discount
Late collection – 15 minutes from the Cuckoo Club results in a £10 collection fee.
Child Care Vouchers are accepted
Two weeks’ notice is required for cancellation of regularly booked sessions.
You can book up to midnight the day before.
In order to register to attend either club please visit:
https://sellincourtprimary.magicbooking.co.uk
Once you have registered your child you can book your children into the Breakfast or After School Provision. Payment is made directly online when making the booking via the above website address. Children who are registered may book an ad hoc place on the day via the school office, only if there is space available. Please note that ALL children must be registered online to attend either provision.
The designated persons are:
Early Birds Breakfast Club/Cuckoo Club ASC – Stephanie Deane
Email: wraparound@sellincourt.wandsworth.sch.uk

Did you know that if you work and pay for childcare, you may be able to get extra tax credits to help with the costs? Further information is available at the following websites:

Year 3 and Year 4 Trip to Petworth House - Friday 25th September 2026
We are delighted to be taking the children to Petworth as part of our geography learning 'What is West Sussex like?'. The children will be going to Petworth National Trust House, visiting the local market town and exploring the gardens.
Children arrive at school.
Depart school on coach for Petworth.
Arrive at Petworth House
Activities to explore the town, house, lunch and playtime.
Arrive back at Sellincourt. This will be approximate and you will be updated on the day via text if this will be any later.
The payment is £6 per child
Although we are fundraising for the trip and FOSSIES are supporting with the cost of the coaches, the remaining payment is £6 per child. If you would like to contribute more to the overall cost of the visit to ensure that every child can participate we would be very grateful.
To pay for this trip please:
Children are to wear their school uniform but can wear trainers as we will be doing lots of walking and the park may be muddy. Children must also bring a waterproof coat in case the weather is wet.
All children in Year 3 and 4 are entitled to a free packed lunch which will be provided by school. Please read the information on the choices available and allergens sent to you by email, before making your choice on the consent form below.
Please note that this will be your child’s packed lunch choice for all trips this academic year. You will need to provide a bottle of water for your child to have with their packed lunch.
Your child will also need a rucksack to carry their own lunch and water bottle.
We will require parent volunteers. If you are able to volunteer for the day, please select the option on the consent form. Please see the Parent Volunteer Agreement. Your child’s class teacher will confirm with you if you will be supporting the trip.
If you have any questions or concerns, please talk to your child’s class teacher.
Please complete the consent form below for your child to take part in this trip.

MFL at Sellincourt
Spanish at Sellincourt
At Sellincourt, Spanish is taught in an exciting and engaging way, ensuring that every child develops a love for languages and gains valuable communication skills. Our Modern Foreign Language (MFL) curriculum is thoughtfully designed to progressively build from Year 3 to Year 6, giving pupils a comprehensive understanding of Spanish. The intent of our MFL program is to spark curiosity about other cultures, equip students with the ability to express themselves confidently, and lay a solid foundation for future language learning. To achieve this, we implement a scheme of work and resources that offer a relevant, broad, vibrant, and ambitious foreign languages curriculum. This approach is designed to inspire and excite our pupils through a wide variety of engaging topics and themes, ensuring that learning Spanish is both meaningful and enjoyable.
Our implementation focuses on the four key language learning skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing. Lessons incorporate a wide variety of fun, interactive activities such as role-plays, songs and games to make learning memorable and enjoyable. This structured, progressive approach ensures that students continually build on their knowledge and skills each year, enhancing fluency and confidence.
The impact of our MFL curriculum is evident in students’ growing enthusiasm for language learning, improved cultural awareness, and the ability to communicate in Spanish with increasing accuracy and complexity.
